title: Towards Trustworthy Artificial Intelligence for Equitable Global Health

bias_targets.methodology: Reviewing and discussing healthcare case studies, including the underestimation of mortality risks for Black Veterans, equitable postpartum depression prediction across racial groups, bias in opioid overdose risk predictions, and negative user evaluations of darker-skinned telemedicine chatbot avatars.

Reviewing case studies from telemedicine deployment during the pandemic, specifically noting how female AI chatbot avatars received significantly more negative user evaluations due to a lack of diversity in training data.

Summarizing workshop discussions on how AI applications risk amplifying societal hierarchies and encoding social class disparities into systems, emphasizing the need to capture socioeconomic features to prevent exacerbating existing health inequities.
